help.title: Stress-Strength Reliability
help.body:
Description
Stress-Strength Reliability answers: "What is the probability that a unit's strength (capacity) exceeds the applied stress (load) — i.e. what fraction of parts will NOT fail?"

Reliability R = P(Strength > Stress)
Failure probability = 1 − R

Supported distributions
Both the Strength and Stress distributions may be chosen independently from:
  • Normal — P1 = mean (μ), P2 = standard deviation (σ > 0)
  • Lognormal — P1 = log-mean (μlog, mean of log X), P2 = log-SD (σlog > 0). Median = exp(μlog).
  • Weibull — P1 = shape (β > 0), P2 = scale (η > 0). Mean = η · Γ(1 + 1/β).
  • Gamma — P1 = shape (α > 0), P2 = scale (θ > 0, 1/rate). Mean = α · θ.
  • Exponential — P1 = rate (λ > 0); P2 is not used. Mean = 1/λ.
  • Logistic — P1 = location (μ), P2 = scale (s > 0). Mean = μ.
  • Log-logistic — P1 = shape (β > 0), P2 = scale (α > 0). Median = α.
Calculation method
Reliability is computed by numerical integration:
  R = ∫ fstress(x) · [1 − Fstrength(x)] dx
which is equivalent to P(Strength > Stress) for independent variables. Integration uses R's integrate() (adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature). When both distributions are Normal, the exact closed-form result is also reported:
  R = Φ( (μstrength − μstress) / √(σstrength² + σstress²) )

Stress bounds (optional)
Integration is performed over the full stress support by default. Supply a lower and/or upper bound to truncate the stress range — for example, when stress cannot be negative, or when only a sub-range of load conditions applies. The integral is re-normalised to the specified sub-range using the stress CDF.

Monte Carlo validation
When checked, one million random draws are taken from each distribution and R̂ = mean(strength > stress) is reported alongside the numerical result. Useful for confirming the analytical integration for exotic parameter combinations.

Outputs
  • Reliability R = P(Strength > Stress)
  • Failure probability = 1 − R
  • Closed-form reliability (Normal+Normal only)
  • Cornell safety index β (Normal+Normal): β = (μS − μs) / √(σS² + σs²)
  • Distribution overlap area (interference area)
  • Monte Carlo estimate (if selected)
  • Overlaid density chart — Strength (blue) and Stress (red) with interference region shaded orange
Assumptions
Stress and Strength are statistically independent. Both follow the chosen parametric families. The selected parameter values are treated as known (not estimated from data) — supply the fitted distribution parameters from a prior data analysis.
